sections.html:
Crown Point is the Lake County seat in northwest Indiana, about 40 miles southeast of the Chicago Loop, and the city covers roughly 18 square miles. The 2025 estimate is 35,616 residents, up from 33,899 at the 2020 census. This is a homeowner suburb: 85.5% of housing is owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $294,800, and median gross rent is $1,485.

With so few rentals, a tired house stands out on a street of well-kept ones. Buyers who finance with a mortgage often ask for repairs before closing, which is a big reason owners with dated kitchens, old roofs or deferred maintenance look at a direct as-is sale.

sections.h2: Which school district is the house in?
sections.html:
Two public school corporations serve the city, and the township decides which one applies. Center Township addresses go to Crown Point Community School Corporation. Ross Township addresses go to Merrillville Community School Corporation.

Buyers with children ask about this early. The city spans both townships, so a property address is the only reliable way to confirm the district. Have the answer ready before you talk to any buyer.

Courthouse Square, Sunnyside and Holley are all historic districts in Crown Point. A home inside one may carry design review rules for exterior changes. Indiana's seller disclosure form asks the owner to say whether the property lies in a locally designated historic district, so you will need an honest answer on paper.

Outside those districts the usual rules apply. If you are not sure where your lot falls, call the city before you fill in the form.

sections.h2: Recording a deed and the sale paperwork
sections.html:
A deed for a Crown Point home is recorded with the Lake County Recorder, who also handles mortgages, liens and releases. The office is in Building A, second floor, 2293 N. Main Street, Crown Point. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone number is 219-755-3730.

Every residential transfer also needs a sales disclosure form filed with the deed. The statute leaves out a few documents, such as mortgages, short leases and certain quitclaim deeds. In practice the closing company fills the form out when it prepares the deed, so you rarely do it yourself.

For most residential sales the owner also completes a state disclosure form. It covers the foundation, mechanical systems, roof, structure, water and sewer systems, methamphetamine contamination, flood plain knowledge and historic district status. A buyer purchasing as-is still gets this form, so fill it in honestly.

  • Order a payoff statement from your lender.
  • Confirm the township and school corporation.
  • Check for unpaid property tax with the Lake County Treasurer.
  • Choose a title or closing company.

Lake County homeowners pay in two halves. The statute, Indiana Code 6-1.1-22-9, puts them on May 10 and November 10, though the state's own calendar nudges a date by a day when it falls on a weekend. Pay within 30 days after the deadline and you add a 5% penalty. Wait longer than that and the penalty is 10%.

Lake County taxes go to the Treasurer at 2293 N. Main Street in Crown Point, phone 219-755-3760.

A parcel that stays delinquent can be offered at a tax sale. Lake County compiles its delinquent list by July 1 or 51 days after the due date, adds a tax sale charge, mails certified letters and publishes owner names in two local newspapers. The sale is held online, and the minimum bid is the full amount owed on the parcel. To ask about redeeming a parcel, call the Auditor at 219-755-3155.

If you owe back taxes and want to sell, paying them from your proceeds at closing is a common route. Try to do it before the sale list is certified. Tell the title company about the balance at the start so the payoff figure is ready.

sections.h2: How a cash sale runs, step by step
sections.html:
The process is short. You contact us with the address and a few details about condition. We look at the house, usually with a walkthrough, and make an offer in writing. If you accept, a title company opens the file, searches the title and prepares the deed. You choose the closing date, and the money arrives at the closing table.

No lender is involved, so there is no appraisal and no loan approval that can fall apart in the last week. Repairs are not part of the deal: the roof, the furnace and the dated kitchen stay as they are.

Before you call, it helps to gather a few things:

  • The most recent property tax statement or the Treasurer's balance.
  • Your lender's payoff figure, if a mortgage is still open.
  • Any code or insurance notices on the house.
  • Names of everyone on the title, including heirs if the owner has died.

If a house is tied up in an estate, the personal representative signs the deed, and the court's paperwork has to be in order before closing. Start the probate conversation early, because that step sets the real timeline.

sections.h2: Who sells to a cash buyer here?
sections.html:
Many Crown Point owners hold real equity, so the pressure to sell usually comes from time, repairs or an estate. A few common situations:

  • An inherited house in Lake County that must pass through probate before it can be sold.
  • A home that needs a new roof, furnace or foundation work that would show up on a buyer's inspection.
  • A landlord leaving a rental in a city where most homes are owner-occupied.
  • An owner relocating who cannot carry two mortgages while waiting for a listing to sell.

A cash offer removes the lender appraisal and the repair negotiation. It will usually come in below a fully renovated retail sale, so compare it with your net after commission, repairs and carrying costs, and ask for the terms in writing. Closing happens with a title company on a date you pick, and you do not have to clean out repairs or stage the house first.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Crown Point house?
faqs.a: With the Lake County Recorder, 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, second floor, Crown Point. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone number is 219-755-3730.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Crown Point?
faqs.a: In two installments, on May 10 and November 10, with the date moving slightly when it falls on a weekend. A payment up to 30 days late carries a 5% penalty and 10% after that.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Crown Point house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the township. Center Township addresses are served by Crown Point Community School Corporation, and Ross Township addresses by Merrillville Community School Corporation.

faqs.q: Do I need to fill out a disclosure form to sell my Crown Point home?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Indiana's residential disclosure form asks about the foundation, roof, mechanical systems, structure, water and sewer, methamphetamine contamination, flood plain knowledge and historic district status. Ask your closing company whether your sale is exempt.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Crown Point house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes are normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, but a parcel that stays delinquent can be listed for the Lake County online tax sale, so it helps to act early.
